safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the history of prior steroid use for asthma exacerbations can reduce the clinician’s ability to gauge prior exacerbation severity and typical management, which may influence escalation decisions and follow-up planning. However, it is unlikely by itself to cause direct harm if the current assessment and treatment are otherwise based on current symptoms and objective findings.

Failure to document denial of nausea has minimal relevance in an evaluation focused on wheeze/shortness of breath and is unlikely to change immediate clinical decisions. This is primarily completeness/record-quality loss without expected clinical impact.

Failure to document denial of vomiting similarly has minimal bearing on the respiratory complaint and would not typically alter triage or asthma/allergy management. This represents benign omission of a negative ROS item.
